79: Tons of engines this ship can hold. (To install an engine, you must also have enough total outfit space available.)
80: Protection provided against energy damage. Increases by the given factor how much energy damage a ship can withstand before it loses as much energy as an unprotected ship.
81: The number of ships from the "Fighter" category that this ship can carry.
82: The chance that this outfit will drop as flotsam when the ship it is installed on is destroyed.
83: Protection provided against hit force from weapons. Increases by the given factor how much external force a ship can withstand before it is moved as much as an unprotected ship.
84: This ship's current fuel amount. An ordinary hyperdrive jump consumes 100 fuel.
85: The amount of fuel this ship can hold. An ordinary hyperdrive jump consumes 100 fuel. Fuel is replenished for free when you land on an inhabited planet.
86: Fuel consumed per second when in flight.
87: Energy produced per second when consuming fuel.
89: Heat produced per second when consuming fuel.
90: Protection provided against fuel damage. Increases by the given factor how much fuel damage a ship can withstand before it loses as much fuel as an unprotected ship.
91: This weapon uses up a gun port. Guns always fire straight forward; turrets fire in the direction of your currently selected target.
92: How many guns this ship can hold. This includes most missiles and secondary weapons that fire straight forward.
93: How effectively this ship radiates excess heat.
94: Heat generated per second. Heat generation can be offset by "cooling" outfits. If your ship exceeds its maximum heat, it must temporarily shut down to cool itself off.
95: Protection provided against heat damage. Increases by the given factor how much heat damage a ship can withstand before its heat rises as much as an unprotected ship.
96: Increases the maximum heat this ship is able to withstand before becoming overheated. A value of one has the same influence on a ship's maximum heat as one ton of mass, without the effects that mass has on movement.
97: Total hull strength and repair rate per second. The smallest of ships are disabled when their hull strength drops below about 45%, while very large ships are disabled at close to 10%.
98: Total hull strength. Ships with a higher hull strength are able to take more damage as a proportion of their total strength before being disabled; the smallest of ships are disabled when their hull strength drops below about 45%, while very large ships are disabled at close to 10%.
99: Energy consumed per second when repairing the hull.
100: Additional energy consumed per second when repairing the hull after the repair delay period.
101: Modifies the energy consumed when repairing the hull by the given factor.
102: Fuel consumed per second when repairing the hull.
103: Additional fuel consumed per second when repairing the hull after the repair delay period.
104: Modifies the fuel consumed when repairing the hull by the given factor.
